title: Fonctions d'activation
summary: Sans non-linéarité, un réseau profond se réduit à une seule couche affine : les fonctions d'activation sont ce qui lui donne sa puissance. Le chapitre passe en revue marches, ReLU et variantes, fonctions lisses (softplus, ELU, sigmoïde, tanh, swish) et la softmax de sortie ; le workbook ajoute GELU et SiLU, standards actuels. Tu implémentes chaque activation et sa dérivée de façon numériquement stable, tu compares saturation et coût, et tu sais justifier un choix couche par couche.
objectives: Démontrer qu'un réseau sans non-linéarité se réduit à une seule couche affine
Implémenter de façon numériquement stable les activations usuelles et leurs dérivées
Implémenter softmax, log_softmax (log-sum-exp) et la Jacobienne de la softmax
Comparer les activations (saturation, neurones morts, coût) et choisir selon la couche
Expliquer le rôle de la softmax en sortie et l'effet d'une température
Tester systématiquement une famille de fonctions avec pytest (tests paramétrés et de propriétés)
concepts: fonction linéaire / affine / linéaire par morceaux
ReLU, leaky ReLU, ReLU paramétrique (PReLU), ReLU décalée, ReLU bruitée
point anguleux et convention de dérivée
examples: réseau 3 entrées → 3 → 3 → 1 qui s'effondre en un seul neurone (livre §17.2, fig. 17.3-17.5) → Ex 17.1
scores A/B/C 0,6 / 0,3 / 0,1 et six classes avant/après softmax (livre §17.8, fig. 17.24) → Ex 17.6, 17.19

mylearn.purpose: Fonctions d'activation élémentaires en fonctions pures NumPy, chacune avec sa dérivée <nom>_derivative(z) évaluée en la pré-activation z (conventions PyTorch aux points anguleux), plus softmax/log_softmax stables, la Jacobienne de la softmax et un registre get_activation utilisé par les ch. 18-20.

api.signature: def identity(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Identity activation (no non-linearity): returns z as float64.
api.returns: copy of z as float64

api.signature: def identity_derivative(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of identity: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Always 1.
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def step(z: ArrayLike, threshold: float = 0.0, low: float = 0.0, high: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Step function: `high` where z >= threshold, `low` elsewhere (unit step, Heaviside with threshold 0, sign function with low=-1).

params.high: value at and right of the threshold

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def step_derivative(z: ArrayLike, threshold: float = 0.0, low: float = 0.0, high: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of step: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Returns zeros everywhere (the jump itself has no derivative): this is why a network of perceptrons cannot be trained by gradient descent.

params.high: value at and right of the threshold

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: np.zeros_like(z) (torch.heaviside has no backward); finite differences are 0 away from the threshold

api.signature: def relu(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Rectified linear unit max(0, z).
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def relu_derivative(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of relu: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Convention at z = 0: derivative 0 (as PyTorch).
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (torch.relu) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def leaky_relu(z: ArrayLike, negative_slope: float = 0.01) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Leaky ReLU: z for z > 0, negative_slope * z otherwise (the book's example uses 0.1; a learned slope gives PReLU).

params.negative_slope: slope for z < 0 (PyTorch default 0.01); must not be 1 (the function would become linear)

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def leaky_relu_derivative(z: ArrayLike, negative_slope: float = 0.01) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of leaky_relu: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Convention at z = 0: negative_slope (as PyTorch).

params.negative_slope: slope for z < 0 (PyTorch default 0.01); must not be 1 (the function would become linear)

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (F.leaky_relu) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def sigmoid(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Logistic sigmoid 1 / (1 + exp(-z)), computed without overflow for large |z|.
api.returns: values in (0, 1), same shape as z; sigmoid(-1000) == 0.0 and sigmoid(1000) == 1.0 without warnings

api.signature: def sigmoid_derivative(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of sigmoid: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Equals sigmoid(z) * (1 - sigmoid(z)), maximum 0.25 at z = 0.
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (torch.sigmoid) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def tanh(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Hyperbolic tangent (values in (-1, 1)).
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def tanh_derivative(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of tanh: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Equals 1 - tanh(z)**2.
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (torch.tanh) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def softplus(z: ArrayLike, beta: float = 1.0, threshold: float = 20.0) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Softplus log(1 + exp(beta*z)) / beta, a smooth ReLU; returns z where beta*z > threshold (PyTorch convention, avoids overflow).

params.threshold: linear regime above this value of beta*z

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def softplus_derivative(z: ArrayLike, beta: float = 1.0, threshold: float = 20.0) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of softplus: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Equals sigmoid(beta*z) (1 in the linear regime).

params.threshold: linear regime above this value of beta*z

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (F.softplus) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def elu(z: ArrayLike, alpha: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Exponential linear unit: z for z > 0, alpha * (exp(z) - 1) otherwise (smoothed shifted ReLU).

params.alpha: value approached for very negative z is -alpha

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def elu_derivative(z: ArrayLike, alpha: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of elu: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Convention at z = 0: alpha (as PyTorch).

params.alpha: value approached for very negative z is -alpha

api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (F.elu) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def silu(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: SiLU / swish (beta = 1): z * sigmoid(z).
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def silu_derivative(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of silu: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Equals s * (1 + z * (1 - s)) with s = sigmoid(z).
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (F.silu) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def gelu(z: ArrayLike, approximate: str = "none") -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Gaussian error linear unit z * Phi(z) (exact, via math.erf vectorized: NumPy has no erf) or its tanh approximation.
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64

api.signature: def gelu_derivative(z: ArrayLike, approximate: str = "none") -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Elementwise derivative of gelu: derivative with respect to the pre-activation z, evaluated at z (never at the output a). Exact form: Phi(z) + z * phi(z).
api.returns: array of the same shape as z, float64
api.oracle: torch.autograd.grad of the torch function (F.gelu) summed over elements; and central finite differences away from kinks

api.signature: def softmax(z: ArrayLike, axis: int = -1) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Softmax along `axis`, numerically stable (subtracts the max).
api.returns: probabilities, same shape, non-negative, summing to 1 along axis; invariant to adding a constant; no nan for logits of order 1e3

api.signature: def log_softmax(z: ArrayLike, axis: int = -1) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Logarithm of the softmax, computed with the log-sum-exp trick (never log(0)).
api.returns: z - logsumexp(z, axis, keepdims=True), same shape; finite for logits up to 1e4

api.signature: def softmax_derivative(z: ArrayLike) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Jacobian of the softmax along the last axis: J[..., i, j] = p_i (delta_ij - p_j).
api.returns: array of shape (K, K) or (n, K, K); every row of a Jacobian sums to 0

api.signature: def get_activation(name: str) -> tuple[Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray], Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray]]
api.summary: Registry: (function, derivative) pair for an elementwise activation, with default parameters.
api.returns: (f, f_derivative), usable as mlp_forward(activation=f) (ch. 16) and mlp_backward(activation_derivative=f_derivative) (ch. 18)
api.raises: ValueError for an unknown name (the message lists the valid names)
api.oracle: identity with the module functions; unknown name -> ValueError

interview_themes: ReLU contre sigmoïde dans les couches cachées
Softmax ou sigmoïde en sortie (multi-classe, multi-étiquette)
GELU et SiLU dans les Transformers
pro_skill: Écrire des tests paramétrés (pytest.mark.parametrize) et des tests de propriétés
notes: Composition standard : 🔨/📦 = 6 (5 🔨 + 1 📦 scikit-learn, PyTorch n'étant introduit qu'au ch. 20). ⚖️ non pertinent. Maxout, ReLU décalée, bruitée et paramétrique sont couvertes en papier/quiz mais pas dans mylearn (maxout change la forme du tenseur, pas de dérivée élément par élément ; PReLU = leaky_relu à pente apprise). GELU exacte : NumPy n'a pas erf → math.erf vectorisé (bibliothèque standard), plus l'approximation tanh. Toutes les dérivées prennent z (pré-activation) : c'est la convention qu'attend mlp_backward (ch. 18) et le 🐛 17.17 piège la confusion z/a. Deux imprécisions du livre à signaler sans le dénigrer : §17.8 évoque « la fonction d'activation softmax vue plus haut » alors qu'elle n'a pas été présentée, et suggère de comparer des scores bruts comme des probabilités (→ 🧠 17.Q12, ✏️ 17.6 : ce sont les rapports exp(z_i − z_j) qui comptent). Le 🏆 utilise MLPClassifier (seules activations disponibles : identity, logistic, tanh, relu) ; seuil de 97 % sur make_spirals à calibrer. get_activation fournit les couples (f, f') utilisés aux ch. 18-20. Le ch. 13 a fourni logistic.sigmoid (sans exercice) et fait coder naive_bayes ; activations.sigmoid, codée ici, en est la version numériquement stable.logsumexp : nn/activations.py peut les réutiliser par import relatif (from ..logistic import sigmoid) ; l'apport ici est la famille complète, les dérivées et la Jacobienne.
